claim: A disposable, zero-credit R-005 route qualification can reach the unchanged destination [140,31,0] in the preserved McWilliams world through a materially different natural geography, without undeclared threat handling or drift of the player, ecology actors, scheduler inputs, lifecycle gates, or destination.
material_proof: One explicitly selected run starts from the preserved bandit_r005_natural_hostile_ecology_v0 copy and proves its bound world, player, exact ecology actor identities, scheduler inputs, and lifecycle gates before native travel. It uses ordinary overmap routing on the west-flank geography—first [140,41,0] to [139,40,0], then [139,40,0] to [139,31,0], then [139,31,0] to [140,31,0]—and records native route construction, travel progress, every threat prompt and its declared resolution, destination arrival, binding comparison, report ingestion, and accepted cleanup beneath a fresh disposable run directory. This qualification has zero certification credit; it only establishes whether the alternative natural route reaches the remaining-path-one boundary without an undeclared threat or identity/scheduler/destination/lifecycle drift.
material_contradiction: a preserved-binding preflight finds a changed world, player, ecology actor, scheduler input, destination, or lifecycle gate
a required west-flank leg cannot be constructed by ordinary native overmap routing
an undeclared threat prompt, combat action, replacement identity, scheduler change, destination change, or lifecycle drift occurs before arrival
the run cannot reach [140,31,0] with a bound native arrival receipt
the run changes the fixture or scenario, uses a replay or checkpoint rollback, or cleanup is not accepted
already_accepted_evidence: Revision 29's fresh zero-credit counterexample constructed the direct [140,41,0] to [140,31,0] route and progressed to [140,33,0], where an undeclared zombie attack stopped it; it did not reach the remaining-path-one boundary or reproduce a final-handoff divergence.

The R-005 scenario declares McWilliams, bandit_r005_natural_hostile_ecology_v0, the preserved player save, the two-actor hostile ecology lifecycle, destination [140,31,0], and fail-closed native travel stabilization.
current_uncertainty: The direct northbound geography has not established a repeatable precondition-compatible arrival at [140,31,0]. No alternative natural geography has yet been shown to preserve every R-005 precondition through arrival, so a final-handoff repair would be speculative.
forbidden_shortcuts: repairing or asserting a final-handoff defect from revision-29 replay evidence
editing the fixture, scenario, save, ecology state, actor identities, scheduler inputs, destination, or lifecycle gates to make the west-flank route pass
using diagnostic replay, checkpoint rollback, segment splicing, raw-save rewriting, debug ecology edits, combat handling, or an undeclared threat response
treating charter creation, route preview, startup, or a prior direct-route report as destination-arrival or certification proof
claiming R-005 certification or R-006 Windows-feel credit
honest_stop_conditions: stop before launch when explicit selected-run authority has not been supplied
after authority, stop and report the first binding drift, native-route construction failure, undeclared threat, unsafe interaction, missing arrival receipt, ingestion failure, or cleanup failure

after authority, seal and finish when the one disposable run either reaches [140,31,0] through every declared west-flank leg with all preserved preconditions or records its first incompatible causal divergence
only after qualified arrival, diagnose a final-handoff divergence if that same run actually reproduces one; otherwise do not repair it
